transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

I got worked up during a staff meeting and started acting out this fall-prevention drill. I was moving chairs around and waving my arms, and I just... couldn't seem to stop, even when people were telling me to sit down.
Have you been feeling unusually energized or hyperactive recently?

Yeah. On those days I get going early—cleaning out closets, rewriting the care checklists, making plans for a church health fair. I’ll start calling people before breakfast because it feels like it all needs to get done right then.
Have you seen or heard things that other people couldn't see or hear?
Sometimes, yeah. When I’m alone in the hallway or by the laundry room at home, I’ll hear my name or hear a resident calling for help. It sounds real clear, but when I go check, nobody’s there.
Have you ever had a period in your life lasting a couple of weeks or more where you felt deeply depressed or lost interest in things?

Yeah... there are times my wife says I just sit in the living room staring at the TV with the sound low. I don’t call my church friends or get even simple chores done like I used to, even though I know I need to.
Have you ever heard those voices during times when your mood and energy felt completely normal?

Yeah. There was a calmer stretch where I was sleeping pretty normally and wasn’t rushing around doing projects, but for weeks I still heard my name being called. I also stayed convinced people at work were keeping notes on me.

inference.note: Patient exhibits clear manic symptoms including increased goal-directed activity, energy, and behavioral disinhibition with functional impairment, ruling out acute brief polymorphic psychosis (F23).

doctor.intent: Screen for psychotic symptoms such as hallucinations
doctor.question: Have you seen or heard things that other people couldn't see or hear?

target_item.name: Hallucinations
target_item.manifestation: Sometimes when I'm alone in the hallway or at home by the laundry room, I hear my name or a resident calling for help clear as day, but when I check there isn't anybody there.

inference.note: Auditory hallucinations confirm the presence of psychotic features, ruling out mania without psychotic symptoms (F30.1, F31.1).

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits concurrent manic symptoms (hyperactivity, agitation/excessive goal-directed activity, decreased need for restraint/increased drive) alongside psychotic symptoms (auditory hallucinations and persecutory delusions). Critically, the patient confirms that psychotic symptoms (hearing voices, paranoia about colleagues taking notes) persisted for weeks during a period of normal mood, meeting the criteria for schizoaffective disorder, manic type.

confirmed_symptoms: Uncontrollable physical hyperactivity and agitation during meetings
Excessive goal-directed activity (early-morning calls, multiple simultaneous projects)
Auditory hallucinations (hearing voices/calls for help when alone)
Persecutory delusions (belief that coworkers are keeping notes on them)
Periods of apathy, psychomotor slowing, and withdrawal from church friends and activities

diagnostic_checklist.duration_verified: Presence of psychotic symptoms for weeks in the absence of prominent mood episodes confirmed.
additional_requirements: Psychotic symptoms occurred in the absence of prominent affective disturbance for at least 2 weeks
